_comment: F-16A Block 10/15 top-level design REQUIREMENTS -- what the aircraft must DO. ★ SCOPE GUARD: this file holds REQUIREMENTS ONLY, never SPEC DATA (what the aircraft IS -- reference areas, AR, taper, sweep, t/c, fuselage envelope, thrust, engine model: those stay in examples/F16A/f16a_L{1,2,3}.json). Hold that boundary: the file is fidelity-independent and will grow with constraint + mission analysis, so it becomes the most cross-cut input in the repo, and one spec value migrating in would spread everywhere. NOT per-fidelity -- requirements do not vary with fidelity level, hence one file and no _L{1,2,3} suffix. CONSUMERS: design_mach -> F16WeightsL2 + F16WeightsL3 (Raymer Eq. 10.10 M^0.25 for W_en; Eq. 15.3 M^0.341 VT; Eq. 15.17 M^0.003 flight controls) and F16GeomL1 (Raymer 7th Tbl 4.1 AR_eq, GeomL1.m:121-129) -- ★ F16GeomL1 READS design_mach FROM HERE as of Phase 4 -- f16a_L1.json .geometry.M_max was deleted as the third copy of this quantity, and F16GeomL1(json_path, req_path) now takes both paths (todo 2026-07-25 Phase 4 §P4-14, resolved); cruise.altitude_ft + cruise.mach -> F16WeightsL3 only, which BUILDS the AircraftState itself for SFC_mission = prop.get_TSFC(cruise) -- no AircraftState is injected. Revives PLAN.md's Step-0 requirements.json, which docs/PLAN.md:178 records as planned-but-never-built. Minimal first version: only what Phase-4 weights needs. Full spec: docs/weights_parameter_usage.md Part A.3.

Sensitivity is minor (Raymer Eq. 10.10 W_en 2775.0210 at M 2.0 vs 2792.2046 at M 2.05, +0.62 %; L3 OEW 15705.33 -> 15725.41), which is exactly why the citation must not drift unnoticed.
